ground_truth.explanation: A diff that deletes every lock from a structure read by concurrent request threads looks like it removed thread safety. It actually replaced locking with the immutable-snapshot pattern: load() builds a complete new mapping and publishes it via one attribute rebind (atomic in CPython), readers take a single local reference and read a consistent frozen snapshot, and MappingProxyType turns any accidental in-place write into an immediate TypeError -- which the new test pins. No reader ever observes a half-built table, and the old version's behavior under reload (readers between two locked calls could already see different tables) is unchanged. The new SIGHUP reload wiring is safe for exactly the reason its docstring gives (atomic rebind of a complete mapping), and every reader -- including the new known_countries() -- takes one local snapshot reference per call. The removal is a correctness-preserving simplification, not a regression.
